text: **dsh-drag-and-drop**（DSH 插件，Web 客户端）：把拖入 DSH Web UI 的本地文件或文件夹解析为原始路径，并写入当前会话草稿。它通过浏览器端全页拖放监听与本机宿主定位路由协作，优先查找当前和已注册工作区，再使用系统文件索引及有限目录搜索。支持多项路径逐行插入、同名候选的内容指纹比对、目录结构比对与手动选择，并在失败时显示提示。适合需要把本地代码、文档或文件夹路径交给 DSH 工具处理的 Web 用户。无需 API Key；安装到 web profile 即可使用，OS 文件索引工具可改善搜索体验。

dsh-drag-and-drop is a DSH Web bundle that inserts original local file and folder paths into the draft. When the browser hides paths, it searches workspaces and local indexes; users can choose among duplicate matches. It helps pass local paths to DSH tools and needs no API key.

DSH 网页端能不能识别文件管理器拖来的本地路径？

浏览器没提供文件原路径时，能从当前工作区找回来吗？
项目里有多个同名文件，怎样确认我拖的是哪一个？
把整个文件夹拖入对话，让 DSH 找到本机对应目录。
DSH 插入的应该是文件原路径，而不是上传副本。
文件定位失败时，我想看到提示并能关闭它。
How can I drop local files into a browser based DSH chat as paths?
Can DSH find a dropped file when the browser hides its filesystem path?
I need to choose the right path when several local files have the same name.
Can I drag a folder into the Web UI and match it to a local directory?
dsh-drag-and-drop 的功能「本地 URI 转路径」：读取拖放中的 file URI，按 POSIX、Windows 驱动器或 UNC 规则转换为本机路径，并去重后插入草稿。
dsh-drag-and-drop 的功能「本机候选搜索」：浏览器隐藏路径时，宿主按当前工作区、其他工作区和常用目录查找，并以有限递归及系统索引补足。
dsh-drag-and-drop 的功能「重复文件辨认」：多个同名同大小候选时比较采样指纹，必要时比较完整指纹；仍无法区分则让用户选择路径。
dsh-drag-and-drop 的功能「文件夹定位」：先比对目录结构，再对最多选出的文件样本计算内容摘要；仍有多个匹配时显示候选供选择。
dsh-drag-and-drop 的功能「拖放写入会话草稿」：在全页监听文件拖放，解析到的多个路径按行追加到当前会话草稿，并对未找到项显示可关闭提示。
dsh-drag-and-drop 使用前须知：当浏览器隐藏路径时，定位依赖工作区、本机文件索引或有界目录搜索；搜索受候选数和遍历量限制，未命中时会提示无法定位。

**A DeepSeek Harness Web UI plugin: drag local files or folders onto any part of the page and their original absolute filesystem paths are inserted into the current conversation input — without uploading, moving, or copying anything.**

section: dsh-drag-and-drop — Drag local files in and insert their real paths

text: dsh-drag-and-drop README · Why this exists：A browser never hands a web page the real filesystem path of a dropped file — it exposes only a local file URI when it feels like it, and often nothing at all, for security. DSH, though, operates on real files: its tools read, run, and patch actual paths on the machine. Drop a file into an ordinary web input and you get either an upload (a copy that silently breaks the file's relationship with its neighboring dependencies) or a hand-typed path that is easy to get wrong.

dsh-drag-and-drop README · Why this exists：This plugin closes that gap on the machine running DSH. It converts the browser's local file URI into the native absolute path, and when the browser hides the path entirely it resolves the file back to its real location — through the current Workspace, registered Workspaces, the OS file index, and a bounded directory search — then writes that path into the current conversation input. The file never leaves its directory.

dsh-drag-and-drop README · Features：- Drag files onto any part of the Web UI to insert their original absolute paths
- Full-page dim + blur hint while dragging
- Supports files and folders; drag multiple items at once — one path per line
- Native paths on macOS, Linux, and Windows
- POSIX paths, Windows drive-letter paths, and UNC network paths
- No uploading, moving, or copying of files
- Locates files in the current Workspace and registered Workspaces first
- When the browser hides the original path, uses the local file index and bounded directory search
- Computes content fingerprints only when multiple candidates exist
- When several byte-identical copies cannot be told apart automatically, lets the user pick the path
- Failed lookups surface as a dismissible plugin toast (auto-dismisses after 8s; hovering pauses the timer)
- Writes the draft via DSH's input-state service instead of touching the input DOM

dsh-drag-and-drop README · Usage：Drag files or folders from Finder, a Linux file manager, or Windows Explorer onto any part of the DSH Web UI.

Release the mouse when the full-page drag hint appears; the plugin writes the resolved original absolute path into the current conversation input.

Dropping multiple items at once inserts one path per line.

dsh-drag-and-drop README · Install：The plugin is a DSH **bundle** (`package.json` declares `dsh.bundle` + `dsh.client`). Install it into the `web` profile with the standard `dsh plugin` mechanism — **no DSH source changes and no `config.yaml` needed**:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:omdsh-dev/dsh-drag-and-drop

dsh-drag-and-drop README · or from a local checkout:：dsh plugin --profile web add /path/to/dsh-drag-and-drop
```

The repository ships its build output (`lib/` is committed) — no build step needed after installing.

> The old README's `pnpm --filter @deepseek-ai/dsh add ...` + `config.yaml` flow is obsolete: under the official profile/bundle model `config.yaml` is no longer read.

dsh-drag-and-drop README · or from a local checkout:：After installing, **restart the Web UI** the way you normally start DSH, then refresh the browser page — the plugin appears in the browser boot manifest (`__DSH_BOOT__`) and its client bundle loads automatically.

dsh-drag-and-drop README · Upgrade：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web update github:omdsh-dev/dsh-drag-and-drop
```

For a local-path installation, run `add` again against the replacement checkout.

dsh-drag-and-drop README · Uninstall：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-drag-and-drop
```

The command removes the package from the profile and from `dsh.profile.bundles`. After uninstalling, restart the Web UI and hard-refresh the browser.

dsh-drag-and-drop README · Troubleshooting：| Symptom | Resolution |
| --- | --- |
| Dropping a file inserts nothing | Drag again and confirm the full-page hint appears. Verify the bundle is in the profile (`dsh --profile web --dump-config | grep drag-and-drop`) and that the Web UI was restarted + hard-refreshed after installing |
| Wrong path inserted when several copies share a name | Candidates are filtered by full file name and size, then content-sampled only among the survivors. If byte-identical copies remain, the plugin shows a chooser — pick the correct path there |
| Path resolution is slow on a large disk | Install the platform index (Linux: `plocate`; Windows: Everything CLI) and keep files inside a Workspace or a common directory. Every search is bounded: 3s per index command, at most 100 candidates, at most 20,000 directory entries per root |
| macOS/Linux: dropping a folder resolves nothing | Folders are matched by name against Workspaces and common directories; a folder outside every searchable root cannot be located when the browser hides the path — move it into a Workspace or install the OS index |
| Plugin does not load after install | Restart the Web UI and hard-r

dsh-drag-and-drop README · Path resolution：If the browser exposes a local file URI, the plugin converts it directly into the operating system's native path.

If the browser hides the original path for security reasons, the plugin locates the file in this order:

dsh-drag-and-drop README · Path resolution：1. The current Workspace
2. Other registered Workspaces
3. Desktop, Documents, and Downloads
4. A depth-1..3 shallow scan within each search root: the root's direct child, the direct children of its direct subdirectories, and the direct children of those subdirectories — this resolves the vast majority of real drops (e.g. `~/Downloads/dump2 11/iotclaw.ndjson`) without walking the whole tree
5. The operating system's file index
6. A bounded, platform-specific directory search

dsh-drag-and-drop README · Path resolution：System indexes used per platform:

- macOS: Spotlight
- Linux: `plocate` first, then `locate`
- Windows: Everything CLI first, then PowerShell

On Linux, when the system index returns no candidates, the plugin also searches the user home directory and mount points under `/mnt` and `/media`.

On Windows, when the system index returns no candidates, the plugin also searches the user directory and available fixed disks.

To keep searches bounded:

dsh-drag-and-drop README · Path resolution：- a single external index command times out after 3 seconds
- at most 100 candidate paths are kept
- the depth-3 shallow scan expands at most 4,096 direct subdirectories per root
- each recursive search root visits at most 20,000 directory entries
- unreadable directories and files are ignored

dsh-drag-and-drop README · Candidate confirmation：Candidates are first filtered by:

- the full file name
- the file size

Modification time is used only for ranking candidates, never as identity.

dsh-drag-and-drop README · Candidate confirmation：If multiple candidates remain, the plugin compares sampled fingerprints from the beginning, middle, and end of the files. Only when sampled fingerprints of large files still collide does it compute a full SHA-256.

If several paths correspond to byte-identical files, the plugin shows the list of paths and lets the user choose which one to insert.

dsh-drag-and-drop README · Candidate confirmation：Folders are first searched by name only. A unique candidate is returned directly without traversing the browser directory; multiple same-name candidates are compared by sorted relative path, project type, and file size. For directories that are structurally identical, content samples of up to 24 deterministically chosen files are computed; if still identical, the user picks the path. Directory traversal processes at most 10,000 entries and 32 levels deep, and never follows symlinks or Windows junctions.

dsh-drag-and-drop README · Candidate confirmation：Each search level first checks the direct children of the search root, then queries the OS index within that scope, and only then recurses into directories. The priority of the current Workspace, other Workspaces, and common directories is preserved.

dsh-drag-and-drop README · Privacy & file access：The plugin never:

- uploads files
- copies files
- moves files
- modifies files
- deletes files

In most cases the plugin only reads file metadata.

Only when multiple candidates share the same name and size does it read a small amount of content to compute sampled fingerprints, and only when large files cannot be told apart by sampling does it read the full content to compute SHA-256.

All resolution and fingerprinting happens locally on the machine running DSH.
dsh-drag-and-drop README · macOS：Finder drag-and-drop and the Spotlight index are supported. Verified in Chrome on macOS.

dsh-drag-and-drop README · Linux：File managers that provide `text/uri-list` are supported. When the browser hides the path, the plugin searches Workspaces, common directories, `plocate`, `locate`, and bounded mount directories.

Installing `plocate` is recommended for faster global path resolution.

dsh-drag-and-drop README · Windows：Drive-letter paths and UNC network paths are supported. When the browser hides the path, the plugin prefers the Everything CLI; without Everything it uses PowerShell to search the user directory and fixed disks.

Installing Everything and its command-line tools significantly speeds up path resolution on large disks.

dsh-drag-and-drop README · Development and verification：The build script needs a DSH checkout. By default it locates one through the `dsh` command; you can also point it explicitly:

```sh
DSH_CHECKOUT=/path/to/dsh pnpm run build
```

Run tests:

```sh
pnpm test
```

Type-check:

```sh
pnpm run check
```

Build:

```sh
pnpm run build
```

Repository layout:

dsh-drag-and-drop README · Development and verification：- `src/` — host (node) half: path resolution, directory walk, fingerprinting, platform search, and the file-locate HTTP route
- `src/client/` — browser half: drag handling, drop items, path locator, candidate chooser, toast UI
- `tests/` — vitest suites for the host and client logic
- `lib/` — committed build output (host + client bundles)
